A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, Algorithms 1–2, Figures 1–17, and Appendices A–I. All substantive material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical experiments on integer least squares, integer compressed sensing, lattice-versus-set-function optimization, and DCA variants in Section 5 and Appendices C, H, and I.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including recovery performance, objective gaps, runtimes, and iteration counts.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 revises the optional larger-neighborhood extension: v2 searches the full L1 ball of radius c; v3 searches coordinatewise increasing or decreasing moves at distance exactly c and requires a row-stable permutation. Algorithm 1 and the reported experimental procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same integer least-squares and compressed-sensing scenarios, including the appendix noise, sparsity, and dimension settings, plus the same synthetic quadratic discretization study in Appendix C.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ADMM, RAR, OBQ, and the Gurobi optimum for least squares; OMP and box-constrained LASSO for compressed sensing; and DCA-Restart in Appendix I. Appendix C's lattice-versus-reduction comparison also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C, G–I retain the same data generation, initialization, metrics, parameter grids, solver budgets, and stopping criteria. No experiment using the revised larger-neighborhood extension is reported.

E4.justification: The lattice-reduction study, noise and sparsity sweeps, initialization comparisons, and runtime and iteration analyses are retained without substantive revision in Appendices C, H, and I.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100-run averages and standard-deviation error bars for the main and DCA-variant experiments, and 50 trials for Appendix C. No uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–17 retain identical plotted content, including performance curves, error bars, runtimes, and iteration counts. The corresponding numerical settings, rankings, and reported findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The paragraph following Theorem 4.5 narrows the optional radius-c guarantee from arbitrary L1-neighbors to x^T ± z with z nonnegative and ||z||1 ≤ c. It introduces an exact-distance neighborhood definition and an explicit row-stability requirement. Theorem 4.5 itself and the appendix proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about DS representability, equivalence to DC optimization, DCA-LS convergence to a local minimum, and empirical advantages on the two applications.

C2.justification: The optional stronger local-minimality assertion now excludes perturbations that mix coordinate increases and decreases, narrowing its stated applicability. Interpretations concerning continuous domains, initialization sensitivity, and runtime tradeoffs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains the same MATLAB implementation information, solver settings, warm starts, Gurobi reformulation, and baseline implementation details. Code-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged, as are the discussions positioning the work relative to submodular optimization, DC programming, and discrete DC methods.

P1.justification: One paragraph in Section 4.2 is expanded and rewritten. Cross-references repeatedly replace 'Appendix' with 'Section'; the overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Typesetting and text reflow shift some material across columns and pages, including the end of Section 5.2 onto page 10. All figures retain their panels, axes, legends, captions, and plotted content.

improvement.justification: v3 usefully narrows the optional extension and makes its permutation requirement explicit. However, it replaces v2's search over distances up to c with an exact-c search while still claiming a guarantee for all distances up to c; the unchanged Appendix F.5 does not explain this discrepancy. Since this is the only substantive revision, its net effect on correctness and overall quality is unclear.
